headline.caveat: incremental Azure purchase commitment agreed in the Oct 2025 recapitalization; no public schedule or take-or-pay terms

realized_to_date.caveat: not separately disclosed; Microsoft's FY26 related-party disclosure ($24.1B revenue from OpenAI arrangements, incl. rev-share) is the closest public proxy

nature_md: Two flows in one contract stack. (1) Compute: in the Oct 28, 2025 recapitalization OpenAI contracted to purchase an incremental $250B of Azure services; in exchange Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal as compute provider. (2) Revenue share: OpenAI has historically paid Microsoft ~20% of revenue. **Apr 27, 2026 restructuring:** the rev-share was made subject to a total cap (running through 2030), Microsoft stopped paying OpenAI a share on Azure-hosted OpenAI-model sales, and remaining exclusivity was gutted — OpenAI may now sell its products on any cloud (this cleared the way for the $38B+$100B AWS contracts and the Google Cloud deal). Microsoft remains the 'primary' cloud partner in branding, but the economic tie is now a large but capped commitment rather than an exclusive channel.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: OpenAI (private) expenses Azure consumption as cost of revenue; the $250B is an unconditional-looking purchase commitment whose enforceability/timing terms are undisclosed. Rev-share payments to Microsoft are a direct deduction from OpenAI's topline economics — now capped through 2030.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Microsoft recognizes Azure revenue as consumed and discloses OpenAI as a related party: FY26 revenue from OpenAI arrangements (incl. rev-share receipts) was $24.1B with $6.0B receivable. The $250B commitment sits in backlog/RPO-adjacent disclosure, not revenue, until consumed.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** OpenAI's committed spend across Microsoft/Oracle/AWS/others (~$748B+ of performance obligations per Zitron's tally) dwarfs its ~$25B ARR — the $250B Azure commitment is unfundable from current cashflow, and Microsoft's receivable ($6.0B) is growing. **Bull:** consumption is real and audited ($24.1B in FY26 through Microsoft's books alone), the Apr 2026 restructuring shows both parties can reprice terms rationally, and diversified supply reduces the single-vendor bottleneck rather than signaling breakdown.

events.title: OpenAI commits to $250B of incremental Azure; Microsoft drops right of first refusal
Second restructuring: rev-share capped through 2030, exclusivity ended, OpenAI free to sell on any cloud
events.why_it_matters: Converted the defining exclusive relationship of the AI era into a capped commercial contract; directly enabled the Amazon equity + AWS expansion.
